subject: general
question: Which gas reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium bicarbonate and sodium carbonate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CO2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)** is an **acidic oxide** that reacts readily with **strong bases** like **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** to form different salts based on the concentration of the gas.
 
• When **CO₂** is passed through a solution of **Sodium Hydroxide**, it first reacts to form **Sodium Carbonate (Na₂CO₃)** and **water (H₂O)**. The chemical equation for this reaction is **2NaOH + CO₂ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• If **Carbon Dioxide** is provided in **excess**, it continues to react with the **Sodium Carbonate** and **water** formed in the first step to produce **Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO₃)**, also known as **Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate**. The equation for this subsequent step is **Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → 2NaHCO₃**.
 
• This process is a classic example of a **neutralization reaction** between an **acidic gas** and an **alkali**. It is industrially significant as it relates to the absorption of greenhouse gases and the production of chemical reagents.
 
• Other gases listed do not yield these specific products. **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂)** is an acidic gas that reacts with **NaOH** to produce **Sodium Nitrate (NaNO₃)** and **Sodium Nitrite (NaNO₂)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Carbon Monoxide (CO)** is considered a **neutral oxide** and does not react with **Sodium Hydroxide** under standard temperature and pressure conditions. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂)** reacts with **NaOH** to form **Sodium Sulfite (Na₂SO₃)** and **Sodium Bisulfite (NaHSO₃)**, following a similar pattern but producing sulfur-based salts instead of carbonates. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH):**

 
 
• Commonly known as **Caustic Soda**, it is a highly **alkaline** white solid.
 
• It is widely used in the manufacture of **pulp and paper**, **textiles**, **drinking water**, **soaps**, and **detergents**.
 
• In the **year 2022**, the global production of **NaOH** reached millions of metric tons due to its versatile chemical **functions** as a strong base.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na₂CO₃):**
 
 
• Commonly referred to as **Washing Soda**, it is the **disodium salt** of carbonic acid.
 
• It is primarily used in **glass manufacturing**, where it acts as a **flux** to lower the melting point of silica.
 
• It also finds **applications** in **water softening** by removing temporary and permanent hardness.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO₃):**
 
 
• Commonly known as **Baking Soda**, it is a white crystalline solid with a slightly **alkaline** taste.
 
• It is used in **cooking** as a leavening agent and in **fire extinguishers** because it releases **CO₂** when heated, which helps smother flames.
 
• In the medical field, it is used as an **antacid** to treat **acid indigestion** and **heartburn**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental and Industrial Context:**
 
 
• The reaction between **NaOH** and **CO₂** is utilized in **Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)** technologies to scrub **Carbon Dioxide** from industrial exhaust streams.
 
• This chemical interaction is fundamental in the **Solvay Process**, which is the major industrial process for the production of **Sodium Carbonate** globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Oxide Classification:** **CO₂** and **SO₂** are **Non-metallic oxides**, which are generally **acidic** in nature. In contrast, **CO** and **N₂O** are rare examples of **neutral** non-metallic oxides.
 
• **Detection of CO₂:** The reaction of **CO₂** with **Calcium Hydroxide [Ca(OH)₂]**, also known as **Lime Water**, is the standard laboratory test for the gas. It turns lime water **milky** due to the formation of insoluble **Calcium Carbonate**, but becomes clear again if **excess CO₂** is passed through (forming soluble Calcium Bicarbonate).
 
• **Stoichiometry:** The ratio of **NaOH** to **CO₂** determines the product. A **2:1 molar ratio** favors the **carbonate**, while a **1:1 molar ratio** (or excess gas) favors the **bicarbonate**.
